notes: Empirical/measurement study of real-world advisories; introduces no new attack technique, only characterizes and taxonomically maps existing disclosed vulnerabilities.

title: KVEraser: Learning to Steer KV Cache for Efficient Localized Context Erasing

title: Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models: A Survey of Attack Methods, Root Causes, and Defense Strategies
notes: Systematic literature review; synthesizes and taxonomizes existing attack techniques from 128 surveyed papers without introducing a new named attack of its own.

title: Prompt Injection Detection in LLM Integrated Applications
notes: No new attack technique is introduced; the paper discusses known direct and (as future work) indirect prompt-injection threats without naming a new mechanism.

notes: Narrative review of LLMs applied to cybersecurity. Proposes no attack or degradation mechanism of its own; prompt injection and data poisoning appear only as summarized prior work.

title: A Brief Survey on Safety of Large Language Models
notes: Survey. Catalogues direct and indirect prompt injection from prior work; introduces no new attack technique or degradation mechanism of its own.

title: PromptGuard a structured framework for injection resilient language models

title: Prompt injection attacks on vision-language models for surgical decision support
notes: Evaluation/red-teaming study. title: Adaptive Multi-Layer Framework for Detecting and Mitigating Prompt Injection Attacks in Large Language Models
notes: Defense paper. Adversarial prompts are drawn wholesale from an existing public jailbreak corpus; no new attack or degradation mechanism is proposed.

title: A pen mark is all you need - Incidental prompt injection attacks on Vision Language Models in real-life histopathology
notes: Names and characterizes a distinct mechanism: naturally occurring visual artifacts (pen marks, handwritten labels, watermarks) in real clinical data act as injections with no attacker in the loop, quantified at 90-100% vs 0-10% accuracy swings. Confidence medium because the label is descriptive of a phenomenon rather than of an engineered technique, and it builds directly on the authors' own prior adversarial VLM injection work.

title: Secure Artificial Intelligence (SAI): A Dual-layer defence model against prompt injection and prompt poisoning attacks
notes: Defense paper. The four attack categories in the literature review (direct instruction manipulation, contextual prompt injection, input data pollution, adversarial prompting) are restatements of known categories, not new techniques.

title: Strengthening LLM Trust Boundaries: A Survey of Prompt Injection Attacks
